models_used.note: Vendor-provenance behavioural port; declares no timing model.

R25=100k, B=4190K sourced read-only from elec/src/modules.ato ThermalComparator's inline comment (citing NTCALUG01A104GA). No Steinhart-Hart table for this part is committed anywhere in this repo; the Beta-equation approximation is the design's own basis, not an independent addition by this harness. 'Temperature' is an idealized ramped proxy signal, not a thermal-mass or thermal-time-constant simulation.

implementation_scope.note: Only one ThermalComparator is instantiated anywhere in elec/src/modules.ato. There is no second thermal-sense circuit for a coil NTC. THM-02 (coil NTC, 120 degC) has no implementing circuit to simulate -- this is a separate, reported finding, not a simulation result for THM-02.

verdict.response_time_reason: TLV3201_ngspice.lib declares no timing model; the ramped 'temperature' driver is an idealized proxy, not a thermal time-constant simulation.
verdict.summary: Simulated THM-01 (heatsink NTC) trip temperature is 99.47 degC (uncalibrated). This EXCEEDS the THM-01 85 degC trip spec -- the divider as committed lets the heatsink reach ~99 degC before shutdown, 14.5 degC past the declared limit. It does NOT match the ThermalComparator module's own docstring claim of an '85C threshold'; it is close to (but slightly above, after correctly accounting for r_hyst loading the pre-trip reference) the module's own inline comment estimate of ~96 degC. This is a mis-valued divider, not an unreachable target: unlike OCP-01's 50A (which is physically unreachable from a 3.3V rail with a 1:100 CT), an 85 degC trip IS reachable with this NTC/divider topology by changing r_ref_top/r_ref_bot -- this harness reports the discrepancy, it does not propose or apply a fix.
